rv.q: No matter how archetypal these characters and familiar their experiences, when played with such subtlety and emotional veracity, they yield lingering rewards in the sad music of memory.
Tennessee Williams’ world of poetry and prose is presented gracefully, even wondrously, in this distinctive production...
This is a fine evening at the theater, not a divine revelation.
What she’s doing now, though, is one for the ages, an Amanda that may someday be spoken of with the awe that surrounds Laurette Taylor’s creation of the part nearly 70 years ago.
...there is a breathtaking display of theatre magic in director John Tiffany's glimmering production.
This bracing production is now at the Booth Theatre after a run at the American Repertory Theater in Cambridge, Mass.
Jones, one of the greatest stage actresses alive, conveys this in a performance that will amaze even her most ardent admirers in its depth and compassion.
It seems fitting that this performance, and this production, will really exist only in memory – but there it will lodge.
It’s a remarkably satisfying trip to a disturbing destination.
In many ways, this is an eccentric “Menagerie,” which is why Tennessee himself would have loved it.

cn.t: John Tiffany's stripped-down revival breathes fresh life into Williams' classic with a revelatory production that critics hail as stunning and transfixing. Cherry Jones and Zachary Quinto lead a superb cast in this delicate yet powerful interpretation.

vs.sum: The Booth Theatre offers good sightlines with a well-raked mezzanine and clear views from most seats, though legroom can be tight. The theater's elegant, European-inspired design adds to its charm, while sound quality is consistently praised. Facilities are average, with typical restroom and concession offerings.

acc.note: 6 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Not completely wheelchair accessible. Infrared devices available.
